cohort: 200 women diagnosed with severe preeclampsia and eclampsia, predominantly aged 21-30 years and nulliparous, at a tertiary care center in Alappuzha, India.
finding: Severe preeclampsia and eclampsia are major contributors to adverse fetomaternal outcomes, with maternal complications occurring in 73.5% and fetal complications in 57.5% of cases, and earlier gestational age at diagnosis was significantly associated with increased fetal complications.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was the predominant mode of delivery (72.5%).
